title: Check before you trust
summary: How to spot wrong answers, invented sources and out-of-date facts before they cost you.

slides.say: Lesson three. The most important skill with AI is checking. Even the best tools sometimes invent facts. Let us see how to catch mistakes before they cost you.

slides.h:
AI sometimes invents things.
It is called a hallucination.
slides.say: When an AI makes up a fact, a name, a number or a source, people call it a hallucination. It sounds confident, so it is easy to believe. You must learn to check.

pts: Very exact numbers with no source
Links or books that you cannot find
Perfect answers to very new events
Different answers when you ask again
slides.say: Watch for red flags. Very exact numbers without a source. Links or books that you cannot find. Perfect answers about very recent events. And answers that change when you ask the same question again.
Use a three step check. Ask for the sources. Open them yourself, because the tool can invent a link. Then compare with a second, independent source before you decide.
Prefer official websites and documentation, original reports and data, and experts who sign their name. A random post on social media is not a source.

pts: News from the last few days
slides.say: Be extra careful with money, health and legal topics, with prices and predictions, and with news from the last few days. In these cases, ask a real professional or use the official source.
Trust, but verify. This habit will protect you more than any tool. Next lesson: how to protect your privacy and your accounts while you use AI.
